verdict: The accepted version softens the paper's central claims rather than adding new measurements. Direct evidence of TRSB and favored Eg pairing become an interpretation consistent with domain-wall superconductivity, and the arguments against fabrication weak links are dropped. The analysis is clarified: a defined ΔITRSB, a new section justifying the remanent-field correction with synthetic data, and a zero-field diode efficiency versus temperature. The old review's heavy experimental requests (field-cooling tests, null devices, systematic error budget, device statistics, strain) are untouched, so referees either did not ask for them or accepted rebuttals. Multi-band superconductivity as an alternative, which the review did not raise, was added.

inferred_requests.title: Tone down the TRSB and pairing-symmetry claims
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely said the data support but do not prove intrinsic TRSB and chiral Eg pairing, and asked for the domain-wall origin to be framed as an interpretation. The abstract, discussion and conclusion were softened accordingly.

inferred_requests.title: Justify the remanent-field correction and show it cannot create or erase TRSB
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely questioned the H0 shift that symmetrizes the data before TRSB is assessed, and the claim that it cannot induce TRSB. A new section S7 explains the method and tests it on synthetic data.

inferred_requests.title: Define the TRSB criterion and separate it from the diode effect
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely found the identity Ic+(H) = Ic-(−H) and its relation to the diode effect confusing. The new version uses absolute values, defines ΔITRSB in Eq. 1 and distinguishes it from ΔIdiode.

inferred_requests.title: Quantify the zero-field diode effect and its temperature dependence
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked for the size and temperature dependence of the zero-field diode effect. A plot of diode efficiency η versus temperature for Ring 2 was added, and the claim about diodicity over the full field range was dropped.

inferred_requests.title: Consider multi-band superconductivity as an alternative
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely asked whether multi-band pairing or multi-band proximity effects could explain the diode effect and anomalous interference. The authors cite multi-band theory and argue such SQUIDs remain Φ0-periodic.

inferred_requests.title: Strengthen the case that the junctions are intrinsic, not fabrication weak links
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely challenged the constriction-junction and accidental-weak-link arguments. The authors removed those arguments, added the only-superconductor argument, length scales and a full-range IV.

inferred_requests.title: Place the result against microscopic TRSB probes
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely pointed out that scanning-SQUID searches for edge currents found no signal. The new introduction cites these as inconclusive.

inferred_requests.title: Present the toy model as phenomenological and support the lobe-period argument
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely found the domain-wall-motion toy model too heuristic for its role. It was moved to the Discussion, labelled phenomenological, and a device without constricted leads is cited as support.

inferred_requests.title: Explain how in-plane fields and current act on the domains
inferred_requests.text: A referee may have asked what mechanism produces the bistable states under in-plane field. The Discussion now proposes weakened pinning and states the coupling as an open question.

inferred_requests.title: Cite related domain-superconductivity transport work
inferred_requests.text: A referee may have asked for comparison with similar transport experiments in other candidate multi-component superconductors. Kagome references were added, but this may be author-driven.

inferred_requests.title: Fix figure references and typos
inferred_requests.text: Referees or the editor likely flagged wrong figure panel references and typos. Some were fixed.

issue_status.reason: No zero-field-cooled, field-cooled or minor-loop test of the TRSB data was added; S7 discusses only magnet remanence, not flux trapped in the device.
The error analysis is unchanged: bootstrap of voltage noise only, no switching histograms, lead swaps or systematic budget.
No same-material or same-setup null device was added; the only new check is on synthetic data.
Overclaiming arguments were removed and a non-superconducting-leads argument and full IV added, but no IcRn, junction-location or 3K-phase data.
The model is labelled phenomenological and moved to the Discussion, multi-band alternatives and scanning-SQUID bounds are cited, but fits, parameters and field calibration are unchanged.
S7 explains the H0 procedure with the correct symmetry integral and synthetic tests, but Eq. 10 keeps the same-field form and no fitted H0 values or with/without comparison are given for the rings.
Zero-field diode efficiency versus temperature is added for Ring 2 only, up to 1000 mK, without comparison to Tc or the bulk TRSB onset.
Still three rings and 'universally observed'; no device table, sign statistics or Ring 2 stage labels.
The strain-free claim is kept and used again to reject accidental-degeneracy scenarios; no strain estimate.
'Direct evidence', 'confirm' and 'Eg favored by the experiments' are removed; conclusions now say 'consistent with' domain-wall superconductivity.
Only a qualitative pinning argument was added; no alignment, out-of-plane compensation or βL.
The half-integer step data and argument are unchanged apart from a softer section title.
Fig. 1 panel references and one caption typo are fixed; the toy-model panel labels, missing panel (d), 'Figure 4' cross-reference, 'yellow arrow' and 'absence of no TRSB' remain.
The caption states the πrin rout normalization and the text quotes 0.73 Φ0, but no effective-area check or uncertainty is given.
ΔITRSB = Ic+(H) − |Ic-(−H)| is defined in Eq. 1 and distinguished from the diode effect.
The RCSJ supplement is unchanged.
No TRSB analysis of Ring 4 is added.
The S17 caption still says no hysteresis below 10 mT.
The Gaussian Ic(B) argument is unchanged.
The Discussion still links a 45-degree domain wall to a φ-junction without the device angle.
Several typos fixed ('standard standard', 'can are', 'resonanse', 'plotted in in'); 'proprieties', 'bistablility' and 'textit' remain.

unaddressed_major.title: Trapped flux and field history not excluded; no training test
unaddressed_major.why: The new S7 opens on vortices trapped in the magnet and explains why a Hall-probe zero was not used, which reads like an answer to a field-history question, but no new measurement was added.

unaddressed_major.title: Error bars omit switching statistics and instrumental systematics
unaddressed_major.why: The error-analysis text is word-for-word unchanged and no new raw IV or lead-swap data appear.

unaddressed_major.title: No matched null control for the TRSB measurement
unaddressed_major.why: The synthetic SQUID examples in Fig. S18 look like a substitute offered for a control, rather than new measurements.

unaddressed_major.title: Too few devices for 'universal' claims
unaddressed_major.why: 'Universally observed in a large selection of samples' is kept verbatim and no statistics were added.

unaddressed_major.title: Strain-free claim asserted, not measured
unaddressed_major.why: The claim is kept and even expanded ('sharp superconducting transition ... absence of ... strain'), and the Discussion still uses it.

unaddressed_major.title: Conventional explanations for in-plane-field bistability
unaddressed_major.why: No alignment or flux-state data were added; only a qualitative pinning sentence, which may also be author-driven.

unaddressed_major.title: Half-integer Shapiro steps not tied to a domain-wall CPR
unaddressed_major.why: The Shapiro-step results and supplement are unchanged apart from a section title.
